title: A Physically Based Storage‐Runoff Relationship for Steep Hillslopes and Its Application to Distributed Flood Modeling
content:
Abstract

Kinematic wave models are widely used to represent hillslope runoff in distributed hydrological models. However, their simplified descriptions often prevent the effective use of observed soil hydraulic parameters during calibration. To address this limitation, we derived a new analytical storage–runoff relationship that explicitly incorporates percolation under wet-soil conditions and rapid drainage through subsurface pipes. This relationship was formulated using an approximate quasi-steady-state solution of the vertical Darcy equation, enabling computationally efficient evaluation without vertical discretization. Integrated into a kinematic wave framework, the new formulation was implemented in a distributed rainfall-runoff model and tested using flood events in a steep mountainous dam basin in Japan. Constraining the calibration with locally observed soil hydraulic parameters used as reference values allowed the model parameters to remain within realistic and observationally consistent ranges. This approach accurately reproduced flood hydrographs while reducing parameter and predictive uncertainty. Leave-one-out cross-validation further demonstrated improved performance in simulating unobserved flood events. By improving the process representation of hillslope runoff, the proposed model allows calibration to converge toward soil parameters within observationally reasonable ranges, thereby reducing equifinality without compromising simulation performance.
